items.title: How worried should software, semiconductor stocks be about AI risks?
items.summary: SK hynix (SKHY) is reportedly in talks with Intel (INTC) to use the latter's facilities to manufacture memory chips in the US for the first time, according to Reuters. Yahoo Finance's Jake Conley and Pras Subramanian are joined by RBC Capital Markets head of derivatives strategy Amy Wu Silverman to examine how the software industry is reacting to AI headlines, comparing it to the internet booms of the past.

items.title: How Far Can NVIDIA Stock Fall In A Demand Scare?
items.summary: NVIDIA (NVDA) stock trades near $212, about 10% below its 52-week high, and it has gone nowhere over the past three months. The company itself has not been standing still. So it is worth asking the uncomfortable question: how far does a stock like this fall when a real shock arrives, and how long would you wait to get it back.

items.title: Intel (INTC) Is In Advanced Talks On Ohio Memory Chip Manufacturing
items.summary: Intel (NasdaqGS:INTC) is in advanced talks with SK Hynix on a U.S. memory chip manufacturing partnership centered on Intel's Ohio fab. Options under discussion reportedly include SK Hynix leasing part of Intel's planned Ohio facility or forming a new joint venture. The potential arrangement would extend memory chip production into Intel's U.S. manufacturing footprint, aligning with domestic semiconductor build-out priorities.
